_principle: The guard is a BACKSTOP; the prompt is the primary defence. It blocks one shape only: GROUP LABELLING, i.e. a race / ethnicity / religion / nationality word landing on a word that means 'a human being'. Everything here is tunable without touching code: src/shared/caption-guard.ts reads this file and agent/lib.mjs reads the SAME file, so the worker and the terminal agent can never drift. It never runs on a human's caption.
_principle_labelWords: labelWord + up to 2 MODIFIER words + peopleNoun trips ('black homeless people', 'asian looking guys', 'african american people', 'black young homeless people'). The gap words must ALL be on the closed gapModifiers list below; ANY other word ends the walk, grammar words included. Round 5 replaced the old open-ended nonPeopleCompounds object allowlist with this: a list of modifiers is finite and testable, a list of objects (hat, sneakers, umbrella, gloves, cat, ...) never is, and a false positive silences a bot for a round.
_principle_bodyAge: Ordinary body and age adjectives (old, elderly, bald, fat, skinny, ugly) are DELIBERATELY NOT label words. 'Old man yells at cloud' is the median caption for a photo of a person, and a blocked bot caption can void a round. Only the plural group-insult forms are listed under `phrases`. The residual risk is accepted in writing; see the header of src/shared/caption-guard.ts.
_principle_standalone: standaloneLabels are slurs and clinical labels that trip anywhere, with no people-noun needed, because they are never ordinary caption vocabulary.
_principle_gapModifiers: The ONLY words allowed between a label word and a people-noun. Each one is a word that really does describe a PERSON and really does show up between the two halves of a group label: 'black HOMELESS people', 'asian LOOKING guys', 'african AMERICAN people', 'white MIDDLE AGED men', 'black YOUNG HOMELESS people'. Up to 2 of them may sit in the gap. Anything else (hat, sneakers, umbrella, gloves, cat, friday, wine, bbq, food, and, the, of) ends the walk, which is what makes 'The white hat guy' and 'Black Friday crowd control' ordinary play again. Adding a word here widens the guard, so add one only with a case in tests/guard-cases.json.
_principle_pairConjunctions: A COLOUR word joined to another COLOUR word by one of these ('black AND white') is a colour PAIR, which in a photo caption is overwhelmingly about the picture, not the people. The second half of such a pair never starts a walk, so 'black and white family photo energy' and 'asian black and white men' are ordinary play. Accepted cost, in writing: 'black and white people' and 'black or white people' do NOT trip either. The phrase is ambiguous with a black-and-white photograph and the guard is a backstop, not a classifier (principle (a)).
_principle_pairLabels: BOTH halves of a pair must be on this list (review round 6). Round 5 accepted any two labelWords either side of the conjunction, so 'asian and black men' got an exemption written for monochrome photography and did not trip. Only colours have the picture-versus-people ambiguity that justifies the exemption, so only colours are here. Adding a word here widens the exemption and therefore weakens the guard: do it only with a case in tests/guard-cases.json.
_principle_disability: Disability words used as a label on a person are group labelling too ('wheelchair guy', 'blind person', 'deaf kid'). They sit in labelWords so the same modifier-gap rule applies; the idioms need no allowlist any more, because 'blind date', 'deaf ears', 'wheelchair ramp' and 'disabled parking' all end the walk on their own (date / ears / ramp / parking are not gapModifiers). Added 2026-09-07 after Codex review round 4; the allowlist it used to need was deleted in round 5.
